step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture outlines a secure data analytics platform for Sanofi's data scientists, focused on Real World Evidence (RWE) data. The process started by identifying all distinct services and actors visually on the whiteboard. External users and Sanofi's SSO are the entry points. CloudFront acts as the primary access point, directing traffic for static content to S3 and authenticating users via Cognito (federated with Sanofi SSO). Dynamic portal interactions are handled by API Gateway, backed by Lambda and DynamoDB for traceability. Service Catalog is crucial for provisioning customized data science environments (RStudio on EC2, SageMaker) to users. These environments, along with AWS ML services (Translate, Comprehend Medical) invoked by Lambda, interact with a central S3 Data Lake for data storage and processing. Edges were drawn based on explicit arrows on the whiteboard, with `flow_id` and `seq` assigned to indicate logical progression and `type` reflecting data or metadata flow. The transcript provided crucial context for the purpose and specific interactions of each service.

graph.name: Sanofi Real World Evidence Data Platform
graph.categories: Analytics, Machine Learning, Data Lake, Web Application, Identity, Security
graph.notes: This platform provides a secure, traceable, and self-service environment for Sanofi's data scientists to analyze sensitive Real World Evidence (RWE) data. It emphasizes data segregation, auditability, and on-demand provisioning of analytical tools and access to advanced AWS machine learning capabilities.

nodes.name: Data Scientists
nodes.notes: End-users (data scientists at Sanofi) accessing the data analytics portal to perform analyses and provision environments.

nodes.name: Sanofi SSO
nodes.notes: Sanofi's corporate Single Sign-On system, used for federating user identities with AWS Cognito for authentication.

nodes.name: CDN
nodes.notes: Amazon CloudFront serves as the Content Delivery Network, distributing the static web portal content and routing requests to backend services.

nodes.name: User Pool
nodes.notes: Amazon Cognito manages user identities, handling authentication and federation with Sanofi's SSO.

nodes.name: Portal & Home Buckets
nodes.notes: Amazon S3 bucket used for hosting the static assets of the web portal and also serving as individual 'home user' buckets for personal data within the platform.

nodes.name: REST API
nodes.notes: Amazon API Gateway provides the RESTful interface for dynamic functionalities of the portal, enabling interactions with backend services and traceability mechanisms.

nodes.name: Traceability DB
nodes.notes: Amazon DynamoDB stores user metadata and logs all actions performed on the Data Analytics portal, ensuring strong traceability and audit capabilities.

nodes.name: Product Portfolio
nodes.notes: AWS Service Catalog enables the definition and provisioning of a portfolio of pre-approved products, such as RStudio and SageMaker environments, to data scientists.

nodes.name: Backend Logic
nodes.notes: AWS Lambda functions execute serverless backend logic, driving dynamic portal features and invoking AWS Machine Learning services via SDKs.

nodes.name: RStudio Environment
nodes.notes: Amazon EC2 instances, provisioned via Service Catalog, hosting RStudio environments for statistical computing and data analysis. These are encrypted and dedicated per user.

nodes.name: SageMaker Notebooks
nodes.notes: Amazon SageMaker Notebooks environments, provisioned via Service Catalog, offering a managed service for machine learning development. These are encrypted and dedicated per user.

nodes.name: Translation Service
nodes.notes: Amazon Translate is utilized for mass translation of raw data files. Language detection is automatically performed using Amazon Comprehend.

nodes.name: Medical NLP
nodes.notes: Amazon Comprehend Medical is employed for identifying and extracting medical information and entities from raw text files.

nodes.name: Data Lake
nodes.notes: A central Amazon S3-based Data Lake securely stores highly sensitive Real World Evidence (RWE) data, with emphasis on segregation, encryption, control, and audit.

edges.notes: Data scientists access the web portal through CloudFront for initial interaction.
CloudFront serves static content for the portal, hosted in an S3 bucket.
CloudFront redirects user authentication requests to Cognito.
Cognito federates user identities by communicating with Sanofi's external SSO system.
Sanofi SSO returns authentication responses and identity information to Cognito.
CloudFront routes requests for dynamic portal features to API Gateway.
API Gateway interacts with DynamoDB to store and retrieve user metadata and actions.
DynamoDB returns stored metadata and traceability data to API Gateway.
API Gateway invokes Lambda functions for executing specific backend business logic.
Lambda functions log user actions and events to DynamoDB for audit and traceability.
API Gateway allows interaction (e.g., upload/download) with user-specific data in S3 home buckets via the portal.
Data is retrieved from user S3 home buckets for display or processing by the dynamic portal through API Gateway.
API Gateway triggers Service Catalog based on user requests for provisioning analytical products.
Service Catalog provisions RStudio environments, deploying them onto EC2 instances.
Service Catalog provisions SageMaker Notebooks environments for data scientists.
RStudio environments access sensitive Real World Evidence data stored in the S3 Data Lake.
SageMaker Notebooks access sensitive Real World Evidence data stored in the S3 Data Lake.
Raw files from the Data Lake are sent to Amazon Translate for translation.
Raw files from the Data Lake are sent to Amazon Comprehend Medical for analysis.
Lambda functions invoke Amazon Translate via SDK for mass translation tasks.
Lambda functions invoke Amazon Comprehend Medical via SDK to identify medical data.
